id_and_class.summary: Prabhat Ranjan Sarkar teaches that ultimate reality is uncaused, infinite, non-qualified Supreme Consciousness (Nirguna Brahman), made up of a cognitive principle (Purusha) and an inseparable creative power (Prakriti). In a cosmic cycle, part of this consciousness becomes qualified and condenses step by step into matter, then evolves back through ever more developed minds until, through intuitional practice, it merges again into its source.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as the Infinite Source and Goal of Creation

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is the absolute reality: infinite Supreme Consciousness, of which matter and individual minds are qualified, cruder expressions.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Matter is Qualified Supreme Consciousness at its crudest, which is why minds can evolve from it. Individual minds are tied to living bodies and pass through successive embodiments.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Supreme Consciousness is the uncaused source; individual minds evolve from matter only because matter is already qualified consciousness)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Each individual mind has a unit consciousness or soul (jiivatma), neither material nor mental, that is a unique reflection of Cosmic Consciousness and gives the mind knowledge of its own existence. Experience is ‘seen or felt’ by the ‘I do’ portion of the mind.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia exist in physical matter before any brain registers them. Objects emit inferential waves (tanmatras) that carry qualia through the senses to ‘appropriative points’ in sensory nerve cells, where they form simulative images on the mind's ‘mental plate’.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Non-Qualified and Qualified Supreme Consciousness; Purusha and Prakriti with its sentient, mutative and static forces; a Cosmic Mind with seven levels (lokas); five fundamental factors of matter; individual minds, souls and reincarnation.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through intuitional practice (Yoga), which Ananda Marga presents as a rational synthesis of Vedic intuitional knowledge and Yogic practice.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Individual minds develop five layers (koshas): crude mind, subtle mind, and three levels of causal mind. The Cosmic Mind has seven levels of decreasing subtlety, the lowest containing space, air, luminous, liquid and solid factors.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Cosmic creation, the origin of matter and minds, qualia, the self, reincarnation and spiritual liberation.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The cosmic cycle (Brahmachakra): when Prakriti's three forces become unbalanced in a portion of Purusha, that portion becomes qualified and evolves a Cosmic Mind and then matter (the extroversive phase), after which minds evolve back toward the source (the introversive phase).
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Minds evolve from single-celled organisms with rudimentary awareness through plants and animals to humans, carried across bodies by reincarnation. Sarkar holds that everything will eventually become human and merge into Non-Qualified Supreme Consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Supreme Consciousness is infinite and underlies everything; individual consciousness is associated with living bodies at every level of evolution.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Supreme Consciousness is the source of the cause-and-effect universe of time, space and persons. In humans, consciousness drives the thirst for limitless happiness that leads to intuitional practice.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Sensory objects emit tanmatras, which pass through sense organs to appropriative points linked to the mind; the qualia they carry form images on the mental plate.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Spiritual evolution: minds evolve through successive embodiments from primitive organisms to human beings, whose distinguishing trait (manava dharma) is the thirst for limitless happiness.
core_claims_and_evidence: Sarkar holds that ultimate reality is uncaused, infinite, non-qualified Supreme Consciousness composed of inseparable cognitive and creative principles.
Matter is the crudest stage of Qualified Supreme Consciousness, which is why minds can evolve from it.
Gauthier argues that Sarkar's appropriative points answer Chalmers's hard problem, because qualia pre-exist in matter and are not produced by the brain.
Merging into Non-Qualified Supreme Consciousness through intuitional practice and the moral principles of Yama and Niyama permanently fulfills the human desire for happiness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Spiritual and intuitional: Tantric and Vedic teaching set out in Sanskrit sutras, interpreted by Gauthier.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Gauthier suggests locating appropriative points by delivering focused local anesthetics to sensory nerve sites in the brain and observing changes in the subject's experience of the corresponding qualia.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The appropriative points and tanmatras have not been identified physically, and Gauthier's proposed test remains a suggestion.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent within its Tantric monism, in which matter and mind are stages of one consciousness. Its cosmology of lokas, koshas and tanmatras relies on intuitional teaching that lies outside scientific methods.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Each self travels with its mind after death to a new physical body when needed, until it merges into Supreme Consciousness.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The purpose of human life is to merge, through intuitional practice and moral living, into Non-Qualified Supreme Consciousness, the source to which everything eventually returns.
